license_required.quote: It is unlawful for any person in the Commonwealth to engage in the practice of optometry or pretend to have a knowledge of any branch or branches of the practice of optometry or to hold himself forth as a practitioner of optometry, unless he has fulfilled the requirements of this act and received a license to practice optometry in this Commonwealth.

age_minimum.quote: A person holding a Doctor of Optometry degree from an accredited optometric educational institution in the United States or Canada, who furnishes the board with evidence that he is at least 21 years of age

moral_character_required.quote: is of good moral character, is not addicted in the use of alcohol or narcotics or other habit-forming drugs

degree_required.value: Doctor of Optometry degree from an accredited optometric educational institution
degree_required.quote: A person holding a Doctor of Optometry degree from an accredited optometric educational institution in the United States or Canada

accrediting_body.value: national accrediting body recognized by the United States Department of Education and the appropriate regional accrediting body recognized by the United States Department of Education
accrediting_body.quote: In consultation with a national accrediting body recognized by the United States Department of Education and the appropriate regional accrediting body recognized by the United States Department of Education, to approve those optometric educational institutions in the United States and Canada which are accredited for the purposes of this act.

degree_level.quote: A person holding a Doctor of Optometry degree from an accredited optometric educational institution in the United States or Canada

school_approval_basis.quote: In consultation with a national accrediting body recognized by the United States Department of Education and the appropriate regional accrediting body recognized by the United States Department of Education, to approve those optometric educational institutions in the United States and Canada which are accredited for the purposes of this act.

credential_pegged.quote: A person holding a Doctor of Optometry degree from an accredited optometric educational institution in the United States or Canada

required.quote: A person holding a Doctor of Optometry degree from an accredited optometric educational institution in the United States or Canada, who furnishes the board with evidence that he is at least 21 years of age, has completed the educational requirements prescribed by the board and is of good moral character

experience_source.quote: A person holding a Doctor of Optometry degree from an accredited optometric educational institution in the United States or Canada

exams.name: Board examination for licensure
exams.notes: Written and practical portions; prepared and administered by a qualified and approved professional testing organization.
exams.jurisdiction: state (administered by professional testing organization under board contract)
exams.quote: To prescribe the subjects to be tested, authorize written and practical portions of the examination and contract with a professional testing organization for examinations of qualified applicants for licensure at least twice annually

exams.name: National Board of Examiners in Optometry (NBEO)
exams.notes: Passage of all parts of the NBEO may substitute for state examination under endorsement/reciprocity provision.
exams.quote: has passed a standard examination in optometry in any other state or all parts of the examination given by the National Board of Examiners in Optometry, provided that the standards of the other state or the National Board are equal to or exceed the standards of this Commonwealth

interval_years.quote: such renewal period shall not exceed two years

required.quote: a license shall not be renewed by the board unless the optometrist applying for renewal submits proof to the board that during the two calendar years immediately preceding his application he has satisfactorily completed a minimum of 30 hours of continuing professional optometric education approved by the board

hours_per_period.quote: a minimum of 30 hours of continuing professional optometric education approved by the board

period_years.quote: during the two calendar years immediately preceding his application he has satisfactorily completed a minimum of 30 hours of continuing professional optometric education

value: at least 6 hours concerning the prescription and administration of pharmaceutical agents for therapeutic purposes (for certified licensees)
at least 4 hours in glaucoma pharmaceutical agents (for therapeutically certified optometrists treating glaucoma)
topical_requirements.quote: a licensee who is certified in accordance with section 4.1 shall be required to complete a minimum of 30 hours, at least six of which concern the prescription and administration of pharmaceutical agents for therapeutic purposes

available.quote: The board may, upon written application and payment of the regular examination fee, issue a license without an examination to any applicant who: (1) is at least 21 years of age; and (2)(i) has passed a standard examination in optometry in any other state or all parts of the examination given by the National Board of Examiners in Optometry, provided that the standards of the other state or the National Board are equal to or exceed the standards of this Commonwealth; or (ii) is licensed in another state and has practiced in that state for a minimum of four years immediately preceding application.

requirements.value: Applicant must be at least 21 years of age and either (i) have passed a standard examination in optometry in another state or all parts of the NBEO exam (where standards equal or exceed PA's), or (ii) be licensed in another state with at least four years of practice immediately preceding application. Board may impose additional uniform educational requirements.
requirements.quote: issue a license without an examination to any applicant who: (1) is at least 21 years of age; and (2)(i) has passed a standard examination in optometry in any other state or all parts of the examination given by the National Board of Examiners in Optometry, provided that the standards of the other state or the National Board are equal to or exceed the standards of this Commonwealth; or (ii) is licensed in another state and has practiced in that state for a minimum of four years immediately preceding application.

exists.quote: To appoint an Advisory Committee on Continuing Professional Education which shall consist of consultants who are optometric educators and optometric practitioners to serve with the Deputy Secretary for Higher Education or his designee.

name.value: Advisory Committee on Continuing Professional Education
name.quote: "Advisory Committee on Continuing Professional Education." An advisory committee established pursuant to section 3 to make recommendations to the board relating to continuing professional education.

authority.value: makes recommendations to the board relating to continuing professional education; board consults with the committee to establish and approve CE courses
authority.quote: In consultation with the Advisory Committee on Continuing Professional Education, to establish and approve by rule and regulation courses of continuing professional optometric education.

national_certification.value: National Board of Examiners in Optometry (NBEO)
national_certification.quote: all parts of the examination given by the National Board of Examiners in Optometry, provided that the standards of the other state or the National Board are equal to or exceed the standards of this Commonwealth

credential_type.quote: To grant a license to practice optometry in this Commonwealth to any applicant for licensure who has passed the prescribed examination and otherwise complied with the provisions of this act.

is_mandatory.quote: It is unlawful for any person in the Commonwealth to engage in the practice of optometry or pretend to have a knowledge of any branch or branches of the practice of optometry or to hold himself forth as a practitioner of optometry, unless he has fulfilled the requirements of this act and received a license to practice optometry in this Commonwealth.

title_protection.quote: to hold himself forth as a practitioner of optometry, unless he has fulfilled the requirements of this act and received a license to practice optometry in this Commonwealth

scope_protection.quote: It is unlawful for any person in the Commonwealth to engage in the practice of optometry ... unless he has fulfilled the requirements of this act and received a license to practice optometry in this Commonwealth.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Failure of an applicant for licensure to demonstrate the necessary qualifications as provided in this act or the rules and regulations of the board.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Failure of an applicant for licensure to demonstrate the necessary qualifications as provided in this act or the rules and regulations of the board.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Failure to permanently display in any practice location a license or certified copy of a license issued by the board.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Failure to permanently display in any location in which he practices a license or a certified copy of a license issued by the board.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Use of deceit or fraud in obtaining a license or in the practice of optometry.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Use of deceit or fraud in obtaining a license or in the practice of optometry.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Making misleading, deceptive, untrue or fraudulent representations or advertisements in the practice of optometry.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Making misleading, deceptive, untrue or fraudulent representations or advertisements in the practice of optometry.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Conviction of a felony or a crime involving moral turpitude.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Conviction of a felony or a crime involving moral turpitude. Conviction shall include a finding or verdict of guilt, an admission of guilt or a plea of nolo contendere.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Revocation, suspension or refusal to grant a license to practice optometry, or imposition of other disciplinary action, by the proper licensing authority of another state, territory or country.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Revocation, suspension or refusal to grant a license to practice optometry, or imposition of other disciplinary action, by the proper licensing authority of another state, territory or country.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Being unable to practice the profession with reasonable skill and safety to patients by reason of illness, addiction to drugs or alcohol, felony conviction under the Controlled Substance Act, or mental incompetency.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Being unable to practice the profession with reasonable skill and safety to patients by reason of illness, addiction to drugs or alcohol, having been convicted of a felonious act prohibited under the act of April 14, 1972 (P.L.233, No.64), known as "The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act,"

disciplinary_grounds.description: Violation of a regulation promulgated or order issued by the board in a previous disciplinary proceeding against that licensee or applicant.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Violation of a regulation promulgated or order issued by the board in a previous disciplinary proceeding against that licensee or applicant for licensure.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Knowingly aiding, assisting, procuring or advising an unlicensed person, or person who is in violation of this act, to practice optometry.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Knowingly aiding, assisting, procuring or advising an unlicensed person, or person who is in violation of this act, or the rules and regulations of the board, to practice optometry.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Failure to conform to the acceptable and prevailing standards of optometric practice in rendering professional service to a patient.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Failure to conform to, the acceptable and prevailing standards of optometric practice in rendering professional service to a patient. Actual injury to a patient need not be established.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Neglect of duty in the practice of optometry, including failure to refer a patient to a physician when an optometric examination determines the presence of a pathology.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Neglect of duty in the practice of optometry, which may include failure to refer a patient, when appropriate, to a physician for consultation or further treatment when an optometric examination determines the presence of a pathology.

insurance_required.quote: To require every licensee to insure liability by purchasing and maintaining professional liability insurance coverage in accordance with the following provisions: (i) Beginning with the first license renewal period at least two years after the effective date of this paragraph or upon first making application for licensure, whichever occurs earlier, a licensee shall obtain and maintain, to the satisfaction of the board, professional liability insurance coverage in the minimum amount of $200,000 per occurrence and $600,000 per annual aggregate.

definition_quote.value: The use of any and all means or methods for the examination, diagnosis and treatment of all conditions of the human visual system, including examination for and fitting of lenses, administration and prescription of legend and nonlegend drugs by topical or oral routes approved by the board, removal of superficial foreign bodies, epinephrine auto-injectors for anaphylaxis, ordering and interpretation of OCT angiography, and treatment of glaucoma; excluding surgery, injections (other than epinephrine auto-injectors), Schedule I and II controlled substances (except codeine and hydrocodone combinations), and prevention/treatment of systemic disease.
definition_quote.quote: "Practice of optometry." (1) The use of any and all means or methods for the examination, diagnosis and treatment of all conditions of the human visual system.

value: examination, diagnosis and treatment of conditions of the human visual system
examination for, adapting and fitting of lenses including contact lenses
administration and prescription of legend and nonlegend drugs by topical or oral routes
removal of superficial foreign bodies from the ocular surface or adnexa
use of epinephrine auto-injectors for anaphylaxis
ordering and interpretation of angiography via noninvasive imaging (optical coherence tomography)
administration and prescription of drugs for glaucoma treatment
vision developmental and perceptual therapy or ocular exercise
methods_authorized.quote: The use of any and all means or methods for the examination, diagnosis and treatment of all conditions of the human visual system. The term shall include: (i) The examination for, and adapting and fitting of, any and all kinds and types of lenses, including contact lenses. (ii) The administration and prescription of all legend and nonlegend drugs, either by topical or oral routes of administration

drug_authority.value: Optometrists may administer and prescribe all legend and nonlegend drugs approved by the board for topical or oral routes for treatment of the eye, eyelids, lacrimal system and conjunctiva (including codeine and hydrocodone combinations, not to exceed a 72-hour supply for Schedule II); treatment of conditions other than glaucoma, dry eyes, or allergies may not continue beyond six weeks without documented physician consultation; drugs for glaucoma treatment also authorized. Drugs for diagnostic purposes include miotics, mydriatics, cycloplegics, topical anesthetics and dyes. Schedule I and Schedule II controlled substances (except codeine and hydrocodone combinations) are prohibited.
drug_authority.quote: The administration and prescription of all legend and nonlegend drugs, either by topical or oral routes of administration, approved by the board in section 4.3 for the treatment of the eye, the eyelids, the lacrimal system and the conjunctiva, including codeine and hydrocodone combinations

surgery_prohibited.quote: The term shall not include: (i) Surgery, including, but not limited to, diagnostic, exploratory, palliative, therapeutic, rehabilitative, cosmetic, reconstructive, refractive, light-based or laser surgery; or the use of lasers for therapeutic purposes.

surgery_definition.value: Surgery includes, but is not limited to, diagnostic, exploratory, palliative, therapeutic, rehabilitative, cosmetic, reconstructive, refractive, light-based or laser surgery; or the use of lasers for therapeutic purposes.
surgery_definition.quote: Surgery, including, but not limited to, diagnostic, exploratory, palliative, therapeutic, rehabilitative, cosmetic, reconstructive, refractive, light-based or laser surgery; or the use of lasers for therapeutic purposes.

foreign_body_removal_authorized.quote: The removal of superficial foreign bodies from the ocular surface or adnexa.

glaucoma_treatment_authorized.quote: The administration and prescription of all legend and nonlegend drugs approved by the board under section 4.3 for the treatment of glaucoma.

vision_therapy_authorized.quote: the provision of vision developmental and perceptual therapy or ocular exercise for aid to or enhancement of visual functions.

value: Schedule II controlled substances prohibited except codeine and hydrocodone combinations (which may not exceed a 72-hour supply)
controlled_substance_schedule_restrictio.quote: The use of Schedule I and Schedule II controlled substances, except for the use of codeine and hydrocodone combinations.

opioid_prescription_day_limit.quote: The prescription of Schedule II controlled substances containing codeine and hydrocodone combinations may not exceed a 72-hour supply.

oral_pharmaceutical_authority.quote: The administration and prescription of all legend and nonlegend drugs, either by topical or oral routes of administration, approved by the board in section 4.3 for the treatment of the eye, the eyelids, the lacrimal system and the conjunctiva

pharmaceutical_certification_required.quote: To require optometrists who prescribe and administer pharmaceutical agents for therapeutic purposes to be certified by the board.

value: Certification to prescribe and administer pharmaceutical agents for therapeutic purposes
Certification to treat glaucoma with pharmaceutical agents
specialty_certification_types.quote: the board shall have the power and duty to certify qualified licensees to prescribe and administer pharmaceutical agents for therapeutic purposes

pharmacology_training_hours_required.quote: graduated from an accredited school of optometry and as a condition for graduation has successfully completed a minimum of 100 hours in the prescription and administration of pharmaceutical agents for therapeutic purposes

referral_to_physician_required.quote: Neglect of duty in the practice of optometry, which may include failure to refer a patient, when appropriate, to a physician for consultation or further treatment when an optometric examination determines the presence of a pathology.

impaired_practitioner_program_establishe.quote: The board, with the approval of the Commissioner of Professional and Occupational Affairs, shall appoint and fix the compensation of a professional consultant who is a licensee of the board, or such other professional as the board may determine, with education and experience in the identification, treatment and rehabilitation of persons with physical or mental impairments.
